newsitem.title: USA: Romania grain exports seen increasing - US attache.
newsitem.headline: Romania grain exports seen increasing - US attache.

text.p: Romania is expected to have one of its best wheat crops in 20 years, and will export an estimated 1.8 million tonnes of wheat and 1.2 million tonnes of corn in 1997-98, an agricultural attache said in a report made public on Tuesday.

In a report prepared by the American Embassy in Sofia, Bulgaria, U.S. analysts said the Romanian government's recent trade liberalization measures abolished and the surplus production "will make Romania an important grainexporter during the next several years."

Romania's grain sector has lower production costs than many competitors, and the government has decided to remove any non-tariff barriers to encourage exports. "Adequate domestic supplies, sufficient carryover stocks coupled with an anticipated reduction of swine and poultry numbers will make Romania a significant exporting country for wheat and corn," the report said.

The outlook for Romania's 1997 grain crop is "very good" because of favorable weather, the report said. Government officials estimate that the current status of wheat crop is "excellent" with stand height and plant densityabove average. Romania is expected to harvest 8.0 million tonnes of wheat and 2.0 million tonnes of barley in 1997, the report said.

Both 1997/98 total production and average yields for corn are forecast to decline from 1996/97 due to late spring weather conditions which delayed corn planting by about two weeks. Corn production is expected to reach 9.3 million tonnes, the report said.
Romania's feed and grain production for 1996/97 was estimated by the Romanian government at 14.2 million tonnes, down 29 percent from the previous year because of bad weather.

The Romanian government plans to privatize or liquidate the existing state swine and poultry by mid-1998, which is expected to lower corn feed consumption in both 1996/97 and 1997/98, the report said.
Wheat prices for producers will be established by supply and demand for the first time in the 1997 crop year.
Agricultural attache reports from U.S. embassies are not considered official USDA data.
